The trust gap

Authentic-looking is no longer authentic.

Generative AI can reproduce a person’s writing style, voice, and appearance. AppKeyId adds a separate, verifiable signal: proof tied to a credential the legitimate user controls.

01

Prove the sender

Bind an interaction to a passkey-backed identity instead of an easily copied surface signal.

02

Protect the intent

Associate identity proof with the communication or action being approved, not merely with a login session.

03

Verify independently

Give recipients a clear way to distinguish an attested interaction from an unverified one.

How it works

From identity to evidence.

A simple trust ceremony can sit alongside the communication tools people already use.

1

Enroll

A user establishes an AppKeyId identity with a FIDO2 passkey protected by their device.

2

Challenge

The application requests proof for a message, approval, or high-trust interaction.

3

Attest

The user authorizes the proof locally. Their private key stays on the device.

4

Verify

The recipient sees that the interaction is backed by a valid identity credential.

A visible trust layer

“Did this really come from you?” deserves a better answer than “It sounded like me.”
